title: cli build: the legacy runtime bundle hash changes on every identical rebuild, because the temp entry path (pid + Date.now()) is embedded in the bundle and its inline sourcemap
body:
Filing gate: ① a product defect with a deterministic reproduction. This is the repro #7651 was closed for lacking ("UNCONFIRMED … needs a deterministic-rebuild repro").
Business reason: `os build` names the legacy runtime bundle by content hash (`objectstack-runtime.HASH.mjs`) so that identical input gives an identical artifact. Today every rebuild of an unchanged app emits a new hash and a new `runtimeModule` ref in `dist/objectstack.json`. Builds are not reproducible, any cache or CDN keyed on the name is busted on every build, and a deploy diff always shows the artifact as changed.
Reader: `packages/cli` (`src/utils/build-runtime.ts`).
Dedupe (open AND closed): "objectstack-runtime bundle hash not deterministic rebuild content hash filename changes every build" → 2 hits. #7651 is this defect, closed not_planned for want of a repro. #20560 is unrelated.
reach: CLI, measured at `756220c4` on a scratch copy of the blank scaffold. Seen across 4+ consecutive builds in two fixtures.
Checklist item priority: P1
type: Bug
QA-source: #26476 · cli.hook-body-extraction-gates · observed beside the clauses

Reproduction:
1. In a scaffold, author one hook whose handler cannot be lowered to a body (for example one that calls a module-scope helper), so the build bundles it.
2. Run `os build`, then copy `dist/objectstack-runtime.*.mjs` aside.
3. Run `os build` again with nothing changed.
4. The new file has a different hash in its name, and `runtimeModule` in `dist/objectstack.json` changes with it. `diff` of the two `.mjs` files differs only in the `// .objectstack-runtime.entry.PID.TIMESTAMP.mjs` comment and in the inline sourcemap line.

**Mechanism (traced):** `packages/cli/src/utils/build-runtime.ts` names the temporary esbuild entry `` `.${baseName}.entry.${process.pid}.${Date.now()}.mjs` `` (around line 201). esbuild writes that path into the bundle as a comment, and into the `sourcemap: 'inline'` map (around line 227). The file name hash is `sha256(code)` over that output (around line 243), so it can never repeat.

**Expected:** a byte-identical rebuild produces a byte-identical bundle and the same name. For example, use a stable entry name (in a per-process temp dir if collisions matter), or hash the code with the entry path normalised out.

Low severity, but cheap and contained.
